title: Module 13 quiz — Production Engineering and Observability
description: Eight questions on logs/metrics/traces, RED/USE, SLIs/SLOs, alerting, capacity, RCA, change. Synthetic BayPay.

questions.prompt: Which three signals are the RED method for POST /api/v1/payments?
choices: Replication, encryption, and durability
Rate, errors, and duration (including a tail such as P99)
Restarts, events, and deployments
Region, AZ, and task count
questions.explanation: RED is request-centric. USE is for resources such as heap and Hikari.

questions.prompt: BayPay’s Module 13 availability SLO for payment create is which number, and what is excluded from burn by default?
choices: 99.99%; exclude all 5xx
99.9%; exclude typical 4xx (except a cohort may treat 429 as capacity)
99%; include every 4xx as downtime
100%; any log ERROR burns the budget
questions.explanation: OBSERVABILITY.md locks 99.9% and ~43 minutes/month. 99.99% is Module 14 architecture, not the default dashboard SLO.

questions.prompt: Which Micrometer labels are acceptable on a payment-create timer?
choices: customerId, accountId, and Idempotency-Key
uri, method, outcome, and coarse status
PAN last four and Avery Chen’s UUID
The raw paymentId on every success
questions.explanation: Low cardinality only. Unbounded identity labels blow up series count and scrapes.

questions.prompt: Priya pages on which class of signal first?
choices: CPU greater than 80% on any task
Any log line that contains ERROR
SLO burn (fast and slow windows) and saturation that predicts burn
A dashboard panel that failed to load
questions.explanation: Page on customer-facing burn and leading saturation, not vanity thresholds.

questions.prompt: A JSON access log for a COMPLETED payment should include which field set?
choices: PAN, CVV, and BAYPAY_DB_PASSWORD
correlationId, paymentId, outcome — never PAN
The full Idempotency-Key as a Prometheus label
Avery Chen’s government id
questions.explanation: Structured logs are evidence. Secrets and card data are not.

questions.prompt: Throughput falls and P99 rises after a release. What is a Staff first move?
choices: Bounce dmgr-east and Postgres Multi-AZ
Quote RED + a resource/scrape panel, write a hypothesis, then open the next gated file — do not max diagnostic on “database” with no quote
Set -Xmx equal to the container memory limit
Declare 99.99% and add a region
questions.explanation: INCIDENT-1301 class: method and quotes beat a lucky label.

questions.prompt: Capacity planning in Module 13 is primarily about which headroom?
choices: A second region’s idle EKS control plane
RPS, heap, Hikari pending, and servlet threads against the 99.9% / 400 ms P99 contract
How many PaymentCluster members Morgan Hale can start
NAT Gateway throughput
questions.explanation: L-13.5 is operational headroom. L-14.7 is failover / DR capacity.

questions.prompt: Jordan wants to merge a metrics change to main at 17:50 with no review. What is the change-management answer?
choices: Force-push so history looks clean
Protected main, conventional review, and a named rollback — a green pipeline is not a merchant-healthy cut
Skip CI because dashboards are “just JSON”
Apply EKS so the change is more visible
questions.explanation: L-13.7 / Module 12: git is the release control plane.
